statement: Before combining atmospheric data, reconcile variable definition, physical units, coordinates, calendar, time reference, sign convention, support, and aggregation interval.
applies_when: combining, comparing, regridding, or validating atmospheric variables
does_not_apply_when: the operation is only bibliographic discovery and makes no data comparison

sources.title: NetCDF Climate and Forecast Metadata Conventions

statement: A time coordinate comparison must preserve the reference datetime, calendar, time zone or UTC basis, and whether values are instantaneous, averaged, or accumulated.
applies_when: comparing observations, forecasts, model output, climatologies, or anomalies across time
does_not_apply_when: time is not part of the claim or computation

sources.title: NetCDF Climate and Forecast Metadata Conventions

statement: A remotely retrieved geophysical variable must be described separately from the instrument signal and must carry retrieval assumptions, priors, ancillary inputs, sensitivity, and quality screening.
applies_when: interpreting satellite, radar, lidar, or radiometer retrieval products
does_not_apply_when: the claim concerns only a directly calibrated detector-level signal

sources.title: CEOS Working Group on Calibration and Validation guidance

statement: Validation must not treat the reference dataset or instrument as error-free; its uncertainty, representativeness, support, and shared inputs must be included in interpretation.
applies_when: validating a model, forecast, retrieval, or instrument against reference data
does_not_apply_when: the comparison is explicitly a difference assessment with no truth claim

sources.title: CEOS Working Group on Calibration and Validation guidance

statement: A forecast skill or improvement claim must name the forecast object, verification sample, metric orientation, baseline, and uncertainty.
applies_when: claiming forecast, hindcast, or ensemble performance or improvement
does_not_apply_when: reporting an unscored qualitative forecast discussion

sources.title: WMO Guidelines on the Verification of Hydrological Forecasts (WMO-No. 1364)

statement: Ensemble members, related models, overlapping forecast windows, repeated stations, and spatial samples must not be treated as independent without a defensible dependence model.
applies_when: estimating uncertainty or significance from ensembles or repeated atmospheric samples
does_not_apply_when: dependence is irrelevant to the descriptive quantity and no inferential claim is made

statement: An association or predictive relationship does not establish a causal effect without an explicit estimand, identification assumptions, confounder strategy, and sensitivity analysis.
applies_when: language implies that an exposure, forcing, intervention, or process caused an outcome
does_not_apply_when: the statement is explicitly descriptive or predictive and avoids causal interpretation

sources.title: IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 1: Framing, Context, and Methods
sources.locator: Section 1.4: construction and assessment of knowledge

statement: A model comparison must report version, grid and effective resolution, vertical coordinate, forcing, initialization, boundary conditions, parameterizations, ensemble design, post-processing, and verification data when relevant.
applies_when: interpreting or comparing numerical weather, chemistry, climate, or Earth-system simulations
does_not_apply_when: the model is mentioned only as background and no result depends on its configuration

sources.title: Earth System Model Evaluation Tool (ESMValTool) v2.0 – technical overview

statement: Research data, code, and workflows should use persistent identifiers, rich metadata, qualified links, licenses, provenance, and domain standards sufficient for discovery and reuse.
applies_when: publishing or documenting data, code, models, or analysis workflows
does_not_apply_when: legal, ethical, or security constraints require controlled access; metadata and provenance should still be preserved where possible

sources.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship

statement: A conclusion must remain bounded by the sampled region, period, atmospheric regime, scale, study design, data coverage, and quantified uncertainty.
applies_when: generalizing a study result beyond its direct sample
does_not_apply_when: the conclusion exactly describes the observed sample without extrapolation
